value.title: Observed death is not an owner close

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Adds to the pending-close actor/incarnation note: a tombstone does not prove that close_seat ended the holdings. F227 lets an already-authorized held close continue after observed-dead, with ownership rechecked and descriptor CAS intact. Compact still skips every tombstone; an owner-close or missing reason conservatively spares the target.

Death without a close deliberately leaves holdings open for revival. Directory views, routes and role sends must exclude dead seats without releasing those holdings. Filter an explicitly addressed instance BEFORE liveness selection: a dead /196 must queue, never fall back to a live /197.

Proof lesson: restoring a saved descriptor through registry.put proves the persistence seam, not the revive HTTP path. A separate POST /v1/revive probe preserved the complete holding unchanged. Independently removing live_seat's tombstone filter failed all three new role-send regressions; the unchanged implementation passed all three.

Evidence: PR #272 final head 55cea7a841f93e8f1565ed368279ce6ff03fa5c9; final-round verdict be54feba982cc40cee6f65e5018c60ea6526c921.
